beats.narration: The final teaching section. Accelerators, deployments, trade-offs — now they connect into one application. And every connection between components is a place where identity, secrets, and untrusted input can cross. The discipline: identify every boundary before connecting anything.

elements.text:
every connection = a crossing point
for identity · secrets · untrusted input

beats.narration: A multi-component app coordinates capabilities. An API request triggers a Claude Code task, which reaches a customer system through an MCP server. Three components, three contributions — and two seams. The trust boundary is where data or instructions move from one deployment environment to another. Content fetched by the Claude Code task is untrusted when it reaches the next component, no matter how well the task itself tested. Never assume a component is trusted just because it worked on its own.

elements.code:
API  ->  Claude Code task  ->  MCP server
    ^seam 1               ^seam 2
  entry request        fetched content
                       (UNTRUSTED)

beats.narration: Least privilege applies to the whole application, and the math is unforgiving: the app is only as contained as its most privileged seam. One component scoped too broadly becomes the weak point even when every other one is perfect. So scope each to what its role needs. The API entry validates input and runs under its own identity. The code task's fetched output is treated as data at the next seam. And the MCP server — the most privileged piece — gets least privilege, with every access logged.

items.text: API entry — validate input, own identity
code task output — DATA at the next seam
MCP server — least privilege + every access logged

elements.text: one broad scope = the whole app's weak point

beats.narration: The watch-out is a pairing session. Dev A: all three components pass their own tests — I just wired them up. Dev B: where does the task send what it fetched? Straight into the next call, as part of the prompt. And there it is: that content is untrusted, and if it carries instructions, the next component runs them — because nobody marked that seam as a boundary. Each component was trusted alone. The seam between them was not. The boundary existed in the data flow all along; it just had no control on it. The seam nobody identifies is the one a steered action crosses.

elements.code:
A: "all 3 pass their tests — I wired them up"
B: "where does the fetched content go?"
A: "straight into the next prompt..."
B: "...as INSTRUCTIONS. no control on that seam."

elements.text: trust does NOT carry over a seam
the unmarked seam is the one that gets crossed

beats.narration: The reflex: mark every place data crosses environments as a boundary, put a control on each one, and when a seam can't be secured — don't ship around it. Escalate to a human owner. Next, the checkpoint completes a boundary configuration. Then: the module's cumulative task.

elements.text:
every crossing = a boundary + a control ·
unsecurable seam → a human owner
